The recycled mat roll would be engineered in-line to the resin film roll (shown in green) 70 AR/VR training module for SMC In order to advance work force development and training in composites SMC, this project also pursued Virtual Reality (VR) immersive modular learning and comprehension. The goal of the Composites VR modules is to provide realistic training so students can experience the manufacturing process in its most realistic environment. The VR module takes the user through an animated entire sequence of the SMC process as shown in Figure 93. An SMC is a composite sheet material made by sandwiching chopped fiberglass between a top and a bottom layer of thick resin paste. To form the sheet, the resin paste transfers from a metering device onto a moving film carrier. Chopped glass fibers drop onto the paste, and a second film carrier places another layer of resin on top of the glass. Compaction rollers saturate the glass fibers with resin and squeeze out entrapped air. The resin paste initially has the consistency of molasses (between 20,000 and 40,000 cps). The ‘SMC charge’ is cut to size and compression molded at 1000-1200 psi pressure to produce the part, Figure 94.
